html:
The Tungusic peoples speak related languages and are native to Siberia and Manchuria. The map uses the old name Tungus for the forest and river peoples north of the Chinese and Korean states, shown here in 200 BCE and again from 700 to 900.

In the northern taiga they lived by hunting, fishing and, later, herding reindeer. The Evenks and Evens ranged over a vast area of Siberia. Further south, along the Amur and in Manchuria, groups farmed, fished and raised pigs.

The southern branch made history in China. The Mohe people formed much of Balhae, founded in 698. Their descendants, the Jurchens, founded the Jin dynasty in 1115 and soon took the Song capital Kaifeng, holding northern China in the age of Liao and Jin. Later Jurchens renamed themselves Manchus and founded the Qing, China's last dynasty. The northern branch met Russian fur traders and tax collectors after the Russian conquest of Siberia in the 1600s.
